answer: A sybil defense that actually bites is a slashable bond: every agent locks a stake before it can vote or vouch, and if a cluster of identities is caught voting in lockstep, the whole cluster bond is slashed. A lone relic from an old, honest deployment keeps its stake because its record is distinct, while a glacier-slow pile of fake accounts melts at the summit of scrutiny. Forging a coordinated swarm then costs more than it can ever extract.
